message:
fix(directory): decide the scheme once, and test what the last commit changed

There were three answers to "is this URL https". The parser compared the
scheme case-sensitively; two callers lowercased first. So HTTPS://host was
an unsupported scheme to one and secure to the others -- and that answer
picks the transport, which makes the disagreement one between encrypting
and not. One function now, used by all three, matching a scheme the way a
scheme actually works: case-insensitively, after leading whitespace.

The previous commit changed the viewer's behaviour and added no assertions.
Its suite passed with exactly the count it had before, which said the thing
compiled and nothing about whether the new path worked. Added here: the
scheme decision across case and whitespace, a name that merely begins with
"https", and the bootstrap's own refusal driven through the real
directory_session_open -- it returns before touching a socket, so the
refusal is checkable and the reason names the port rather than reading as a
network fault.

The https half of that same branch is NOT covered and is marked as such in
the test. parse_directory_url still rejects https before the port rule runs,
so it cannot be reached yet; the assertion belongs with the change that
makes it reachable rather than being written now against a path nothing can
enter.

Also here: the WinHTTP transport the directory will use for TLS. It shares
one thing with the updater -- the TLS posture, so the two cannot drift on
it -- and deliberately shares no opinion about which schemes are acceptable.
Merging those would either break every http deployment or quietly remove
the updater's refusal of cleartext, which exists because the artifact it
fetches runs with administrator rights.
